links.outcome: Worst-case and macro accuracy under poisoned retrieved evidence and reasoning chains, router vs fixed strategies
links.effect: Med-TrustRouter reached 78.9 macro and 69.2 worst-case accuracy, matching the strongest competitor on macro accuracy while substantially improving the worst-case floor.
links.quote: Across seven medical reasoning settings, Med-TrustRouter achieves 78.9 macro and 69.2 worst-case accuracy, matching the strongest competitor on macro accuracy while substantially improving the worst-case floor.

links.outcome: Robustness of RAG grounding to poisoned evidence versus accuracy when evidence is useful
links.effect: No fixed knowledge-use strategy was robust; strong RAG methods traded robustness to poisoned evidence against accuracy when evidence was useful.
links.quote: No fixed knowledge-use strategy is robust across these settings: strong RAG methods trade robustness to poisoned evidence against accuracy when evidence is useful.

unlisted_practices: Learned per-instance routing controller that decides when to trust external knowledge and preserves the base answer unless another action is confidently better (regression-safe routing)

screen.reason: The study develops a benchmark for knowledge poisoning in clinical LLM reasoning and tests a runtime safeguard/controller (Med-TrustRouter) that routes whether to trust external retrieved knowledge to prevent performance regressions.

primary.practice: regression-safe routing for retrieved knowledge / input filtering guardrail
